probes.name: PA
probes.subject: tools/check_ac_consistency.py
probes.note: Removes the implementation-module exemption entirely — the pre-s283 behaviour that accused PLAN-0122 AC-10. The covered case must redden, which is what makes the new rule load-bearing rather than decorative. The other two assertions stay green because neither exempts anything: in the control nothing is covered, and in the second-test case the reported module is a test module, which this branch never exempted.

probes.name: PB
probes.subject: tools/check_ac_consistency.py
probes.expect_claim: test_a_second_test_module_missing_from_the_denominator_is_still_found|[(g.ac, "test_uncovered.py" in g.reason) for g in gaps] == [(1, True)]|#0
probes.note: Widens the exemption to TEST modules too. A test module carries claims, so exempting one hides an uncovered half of the denominator — the exact under-counting Check 3 exists to stop. Reddens the second-test assertion alone: the covered case still reports nothing, and the control has no covered test module to trigger the widened branch.

probes.name: PC
probes.subject: tools/check_ac_consistency.py
probes.old: covered_by_a_test = any(m.startswith("test_") and m in sources for m in modules)
probes.note: Makes the exemption unconditional — the failure mode where the rule goes blind and every implementation artifact passes regardless of evidence. Reddens the positive control, which is the assertion whose whole job is to prove the exemption still has an off state. The covered case stays green (it was already covered) and the second-test case stays green (its reported module is a test module, still not exempted).
